researched_by: the Authority's own parking, wild camping and dark skies pages, its published car parking spaces schedule, its model publication scheme, its Astronomer's Guide to Exmoor, and its 2023 car park charging consultation
policy_summary:
Exmoor prohibits overnight parking and camping in its own car parks, and it does so with one parenthesis of small print. The parking page's terms and conditions read: 'Standard terms and conditions for parking apply (e.g. no overnight parking or camping)'. That is the entire published rule. There is no byelaw, no off-street parking order, no PSPO and no traffic order behind it. The Authority's own model publication scheme lists Byelaws as a class of information and annotates it 'Link still to be added if applicable' - Exmoor appears simply not to have any. Twenty-five miles south, Dartmoor prohibits exactly the same thing by byelaw, which is local criminal law. Exmoor prohibits it by conditions of entry, which is contract and trespass. Same words, entirely different legal weight, and the reason it matters is that a landowner's condition cannot be enforced by penalty charge or prosecution - only by asking you to leave.

The estate is small. Five pay and display car parks (Ashcombe at Simonsbath, Exmoor House at Dulverton weekends only, Haddon Hill, Tarr Steps main car park, and Valley of Rocks at Lynton), nine free ones (Blackmoor Gate, Cussacombe Gate, Exford, Marsh Bridge, North Hill in two parts, Robbers Bridge, Porlock Common, Woody Bay, Anstey Gate), and about 585 spaces in total. Charges apply 10am to 6pm, cash and card. There is exactly one permit product, a GBP65 annual day-parking permit valid in four car parks. No motorhome bay, no aire, no overnight permit, no waste disposal point, no self-containment scheme. Exmoor has made no provision of any kind.

NO CLOSURE INSTRUMENT WAS FOUND. The register expected opening hours to do the work here, and they do not. Nothing on the Authority's pages, in its car park schedule or in its own night-time guidance describes gates, barriers or locking times at any ENPA car park. They are unbarriered rural surfaces, open all night, with the tariff simply switching off at 6pm.

AND THAT IS DELIBERATE, because of the dark sky. Exmoor became Europe's first International Dark Sky Reserve in 2011 and the Authority actively wants people out in it after dark. Its own Astronomer's Guide names five observing sites and gives parking notes for each: Haddon Hill - its own pay and display car park, 'a large flat, circular area', with toilets - plus Porlock Common, which is its own free car park, and Dunkery Beacon, Brendon Two Gates and Molland Moor. It hires out telescopes from its visitor centres and runs a Dark Skies Festival each autumn. So the Authority is publishing directions to its own car parks for use at two in the morning while its parking page forbids staying the night in them.

That is not a contradiction, it is the cleanest parking-versus-sleeping split in the dataset. Presence at night is encouraged. Occupancy overnight is not. A van at Haddon Hill at 3am with a telescope out is doing precisely what the Authority asks; the same van with the blinds down and someone asleep in it is in breach of the conditions of entry. Nothing published draws the line explicitly, but the two documents together draw it clearly enough.

Off the car parks there is no right to stay. Exmoor has nothing equivalent to Dartmoor's wild camping right - not even for tents. The Authority's guidance is blunt: 'you must seek landowner permission before parking up or pitching overnight on Exmoor - no matter how remote the location may seem', with a specific warning that spots recommended on social media 'may not have land owner consent'.

SCOPE WARNING. Most of the Exmoor car parks a van user would actually head for are not the Authority's. County Gate, Webbers Post, Horner, Bossington, Hunters Inn/Heddon Valley and Malsmead are NATIONAL TRUST. Dulverton (Lion and Guildhall), Dunster (Steep and West Street) and Porlock (Doverhay and Central) are SOMERSET COUNCIL. Nutcombe Bottom is Forestry England, Wimbleball is South West Lakes, Porlock Weir and Porlock Hill are the Porlock Manor Estate, and the Lynton, Lynmouth and Valley of Rocks town car parks sit in North Devon. The National Trust ones carry the Trust's national no-overnight-parking rule and are recorded in national-trust.json; the roads are Devon County Council's and Somerset's. Nothing in this file is about any of those.
notes:
The register's premise needs correcting. Exmoor National Park Authority does NOT own County Gate, Webbers Post or Dunkery - the Authority's own parking page lists County Gate and Webbers Post as National Trust car parks, and Dunkery Beacon parking is Holnicote Estate, also National Trust. Landacre does not appear in the Authority's published car park schedule at all; the parking there is roadside on Withypool Common, which is common land rather than ENPA freehold. Of the places named in the brief, only Haddon Hill is genuinely the Authority's, and the Lynmouth-area holding is Valley of Rocks, which is in Lynton rather than Lynmouth. One oddity worth keeping: the Authority's own Car parking spaces PDF still lists County Gate (47 spaces) and Haddon Hill among its free car parks, which the live parking page contradicts on both counts. The PDF is stale.

The instrument finding is the substantive one. This is the first national park in the dataset that prohibits overnight stays with no legal instrument behind the prohibition at all. Dartmoor has byelaws; the Peak District has car park byelaws; Northumberland and the Lake District have parking orders. Exmoor has a parenthesis. That has a practical consequence a user should understand: the realistic worst case in an ENPA car park is a ranger knocking on the window, not a PCN and not a summons. It also means the rule could be changed by an officer editing a web page, in either direction, with no consultation and no order.

Enforcement reality is thin and mostly about the moor rather than the car parks. The one first-hand account found describes new no-overnight-camping signs on the open moor with police cars and rangers patrolling and 'not just a token gesture' - but that is a visitor's forum post of uncertain date, probably from the 2020-21 pressure period, and it concerns moorland rather than ENPA car parks. Nothing suggests a systematic night patrol of the fourteen car parks, most of which are miles from anywhere.

Direction of travel: charging is expanding, the overnight rule is static. The Authority consulted in July 2023 on introducing GBP3/GBP5 charges at Haddon Hill and Exford, explicitly because 'our current government funding is around half of what it was 10 years ago', and launched the annual permit at the same time. Haddon Hill now charges; Exford is still listed as free. Not one word of that programme addressed motorhomes, overnight use or anti-social behaviour in car parks. Exmoor is monetising daytime parking under financial pressure and has not engaged with overnight demand as an issue in either direction. It is the quietest national park in the dataset on this subject.

The dark sky point deserves to survive into the product. Exmoor is the clearest case anywhere in the dataset where an authority's tourism proposition and its parking small print pull against each other, and where the honest advice is genuinely nuanced: go, at night, to these exact car parks, with the Authority's blessing - and then drive somewhere else to sleep.
open_questions: Where do the 'standard terms and conditions for parking' actually live? The parking page cites them but links nothing, and no separate T&C document, signage wording or car park byelaw could be found anywhere on the Authority's site. Somebody should ask ENPA for the document and for a photograph of a car park sign.

Does Exmoor National Park Authority have byelaws at all? The model publication scheme lists Byelaws as a class with 'Link still to be added if applicable', which reads as 'no'. Confirming this with the Authority would settle the biggest legal question in this file.
Is any ENPA car park gated or locked overnight? Nothing found says so, and the dark skies material implies not, but this was proved only by absence of evidence.

Exmoor House, Dulverton is listed by ENPA as its own pay and display 'weekends only' while Somerset Council publishes the same car park as its own, charging 9am-6pm daily. Two adjacent car parks, a shared site, or a weekday/weekend split? Unresolved.
Exford was consulted on for charging in July 2023 alongside Haddon Hill. Haddon Hill now charges; the parking page still lists Exford as free. Was the Exford proposal dropped?
Is the moorland 'no overnight camping' signage described by visitors an ENPA scheme, a landowner scheme, or a police one, and is it still in place in 2026?

Who owns and controls the Landacre Bridge parking on Withypool Common, and is there any restriction there? It is one of the best-known informal stopping places on Exmoor and it is not in the ENPA schedule.
Are there vehicle length, weight or height limits at any ENPA car park? None are published, and several are narrow-laned moorland sites where a large motorhome would struggle regardless.

sites.name: All Exmoor National Park Authority car parks
sites.notes: The estate-wide rule, and the whole of it: 'Standard terms and conditions for parking apply (e.g. no overnight parking or camping)', from the Authority's parking page. It covers all fourteen ENPA car parks, paid and free alike. Recorded as landowner policy rather than byelaw or parking order because no such instrument exists - the Authority's model publication scheme lists Byelaws with the annotation 'Link still to be added if applicable'. The prohibition therefore bites as a condition of entry, enforceable by asking you to leave, not by penalty charge or prosecution. It catches parking AND camping, so it is not restricted to occupied vehicles on its face, though enforcement in practice will be. Charges apply 10am to 6pm only; the tariff stopping at 6pm does not lift the overnight condition.

sites.name: Haddon Hill Car Park
sites.search_hint: Haddon Hill car park, Exmoor, near Wimbleball Lake
sites.notes: THE DARK SKY CASE IN ONE CAR PARK. The Authority's own Astronomer's Guide to Exmoor names Haddon Hill as one of five recommended observing sites - 'Parking is available in a large flat, circular area', with toilets on site, the only one of the five that has them. It is unbarriered and open all night, and the Authority is actively inviting people to use it after dark. It is also covered by the estate-wide no overnight parking or camping condition. So: come at midnight, encouraged; stay until morning, not permitted. The time_from and time_to fields record the unpriced window (charges run 10am-6pm), not a closure - there is no closure. Charging was introduced here following a July 2023 consultation at GBP3 for 3 hours and GBP5 for longer; it appears in the Authority's older car parking spaces schedule as a free car park with 45 spaces, which is now out of date. Included in the GBP65 annual permit.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of TA4 2DS, the postcode the Authority publishes for Haddon Hill car park, on the ridge above Wimbleball Lake

sites.name: Valley of Rocks Car Park, Lynton
sites.search_hint: Valley of Rocks car park, Lynton
sites.notes: The Authority's only coastal car park and its most visited, at the head of the Valley of Rocks west of Lynton. Pay and display 10am-6pm, cash and card, included in the GBP65 annual permit, covered by the estate-wide no overnight parking or camping condition. THIS IS THE LYNTON AND LYNMOUTH PRESSURE POINT AND IT IS SPLIT THREE WAYS: this car park is ENPA's, the Lynton and Lynmouth town car parks are listed separately as partner-operated, and the only place in the two villages where a motorhome may legitimately stay the night is Bottom Meadow, which is North Devon Council's - three designated motorhome bays at GBP16 a night. A van refused here has somewhere to go, but it belongs to a different authority and neither council's page says so.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of EX35 6JH, the postcode the Authority publishes for the Valley of Rocks car park

sites.name: Tarr Steps Car Park (main car park)
sites.search_hint: Tarr Steps main car park, Exmoor
sites.notes: The largest single ENPA car park, 120 marked spaces serving the medieval clapper bridge over the Barle. Pay and display 10am-6pm; the permit and the charge apply to the MAIN car park only, which is up the hill from the steps - the lower approach is a narrow single-track lane and is not the parking. Covered by the estate-wide no overnight parking or camping condition.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of TA22 9PY, the postcode the Authority publishes for Tarr Steps; the main car park sits a few hundred metres uphill from the clapper bridge itself

sites.name: Ashcombe Car Park, Simonsbath
sites.notes: 54 unmarked spaces at Simonsbath in the middle of the moor, on the B3223/B3358. Pay and display 10am-6pm, included in the GBP65 annual permit. Covered by the estate-wide no overnight parking or camping condition. Listed as a free car park in the Authority's older car parking spaces schedule, which predates the current charging regime.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of TA24 7SH, the postcode the Authority publishes for Ashcombe car park, at Simonsbath

sites.name: Exmoor House Car Park, Dulverton
sites.notes: The Authority's headquarters car park in Dulverton, listed as ENPA pay and display WEEKENDS ONLY. Confidence is medium because Somerset Council publishes a car park of the same name at Dulverton as its own, charging 9am-6pm daily at GBP1.00 to GBP5.80 with season tickets - so either the site is shared on a weekday/weekend basis or there are two adjacent car parks and the ENPA page and the Somerset page are describing different ground. Covered by the ENPA no overnight parking or camping condition to the extent it is ENPA's; if it is Somerset's, Somerset's rules apply and this record should be reassigned.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of TA22 9HL, the postcode both the Authority and Somerset Council publish for Exmoor House, Dulverton

sites.name: All Exmoor National Park Authority free car parks (Blackmoor Gate, Cussacombe Gate, Exford, Marsh Bridge, North Hill, Robbers Bridge, Porlock Common, Woody Bay, Anstey Gate)
sites.notes: THE TRAP IN THIS FILE. Nine ENPA car parks with no charge, no barrier, no machine and in most cases no attendant within ten miles - Blackmoor Gate, Cussacombe Gate, Exford (30 marked spaces), Marsh Bridge, North Hill at Moor Wood (98 spaces) and Burgundy Combe (12), Robbers Bridge (45), Porlock Common (23), Woody Bay (8) and Anstey Gate (10). Free is not the same as permitted: the estate-wide 'no overnight parking or camping' condition applies to these exactly as it does to the paid ones, and a free unbarriered moorland car park with a sea view is precisely where an unbriefed van will stop. Porlock Common is one of the five sites the Authority's own Astronomer's Guide recommends for night observing, so it is simultaneously somewhere you are invited to be at 2am and somewhere you may not sleep. Exford was consulted on for charging in 2023 and is still listed free. No single coordinate is honest for nine scattered sites.

sites.name: Open moorland, roadside and lay-bys throughout Exmoor National Park
sites.notes: NO WILD CAMPING RIGHT EXISTS ON EXMOOR - not for vehicles and, unlike Dartmoor, not for tents either. The Authority's guidance is that 'you must seek landowner permission before parking up or pitching overnight on Exmoor - no matter how remote the location may seem', with a specific warning that spots recommended on social media may not have the landowner's consent. The control is ordinary land law: staying without permission is trespass, a civil matter, and there is no Exmoor byelaw creating an offence of sleeping in a vehicle. That is the sharp contrast with Dartmoor twenty-five miles south, where the same conduct breaches a byelaw and is a criminal matter. Recorded as policy_only rather than landowner_policy because the Authority is stating the general legal position across land it mostly does not own, not imposing its own condition. Enforcement is unclear: one visitor account describes new no-overnight-camping signage on the moor being patrolled by police and rangers and 'not just a token gesture', but the account is undated and probably from the 2020-21 pressure period, and it concerns the open moor rather than car parks. Devon County Council and Somerset are the highway authorities for the roads and lay-bys; no motor caravan waiting restriction was found on any Exmoor road in Devon's Schedule 14.
